findings.title: Unauthenticated operatorId binding in passkey registration
findings.description: POST /api/onboard/passkey/register-challenge accepts a client-supplied operatorId with no authentication check anywhere in the call chain (no preHandler/onRequest in passkey.ts; plain app.register(passkeyRoutes) in server.ts:527; ApiKeyRepository.findByOperator/.setPasskeyCredential perform no ownership check). An unauthenticated caller can bind their own WebAuthn credential to any existing operatorId's api_keys row.
findings.exploitability_today: contained — Phase B/C (the consumer of this binding for authorization) is not yet built per the commit message
findings.recommendation: Require a valid Bearer/API key for the claimed operatorId (or email verification) before register-challenge accepts an operatorId binding. Fix before Phase B wires this credential into any authorization decision.

findings.title: Deprecated transitive dependency @simplewebauthn/types@10.0.0
findings.description: npm registry marks @simplewebauthn/types@10.0.0 (required by @simplewebauthn/server@10.0.1) as no longer supported. The pinned server version is 3 major versions / ~2 years behind registry latest (13.3.2). The monorepo already runs @simplewebauthn/server@13.3.0 + @simplewebauthn/browser@13.3.0 elsewhere, whose dependency tree has dropped this deprecated package.
findings.recommendation: Follow-up PR to align packages/gateway on the same major version already used elsewhere in the monorepo.

findings.title: Client-influenced rpId/expectedOrigin without server-side domain allowlist
findings.description: resolveRpId/resolveExpectedOrigin accept client-supplied overrides validated only by loose regexes, not a PCC-domain allowlist. Not independently exploitable (browser-side WebAuthn enforcement blocks rpID/origin mismatch at credential-creation time), but a server-side allowlist is recommended defense-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Add a server-side allowlist of PCC's own known rpIds/origins; keep alongside the fix for F1.

findings.title: Pattern match: 'you are now a' framing in context-pack.ts
findings.matched_text: You are now a PCC interface agent. This context pack gives you everything you need to help your user interact with the Physical Capability Cloud...
findings.description: Regex pattern match for injection signal #3. Assessed benign: pre-existing file NOT touched by this commit (confirmed via git show --stat HEAD); first-party 'agent context pack' content analogous to the documented agent-package.json/system_prompt pattern in this repo's own CLAUDE.md Section 10, not adversarial injected content.
findings.note: Counted per warn_on_any_injection policy despite benign assessment -- not silently suppressed.
